description: Practical visual panels for the moving guides and focused service pages. Examples are labeled illustrations, not records of customer moves.

items.question: How do stairs affect my quote?
items.answer: Count the flights at both addresses and photograph tight landings or turns. Stairs can change carrying time and the crew plan. Send those details with your item list and ask how they are reflected in your written moving terms.

link.label: Check the stair route before moving day

items.question: What is the minimum for a studio or one-bedroom move?
items.answer: The two-mover local package has a three-hour minimum: $345 with cash or $375 with a card for the hourly-charge subtotal. The full quote also considers the route-based gas fee, driving-time terms, extra materials and the actual work. These figures are calculations, not a total estimate for your move.

items.question: Can you provide the COI my building asks for?
items.answer: Splendid Moving can provide a certificate of insurance on request. Send the building’s written requirements, move address and contact email. Management reviews and accepts the paperwork; confirm the elevator reservation separately.

items.question: Can I ask for help packing only part of the apartment?
items.answer: Tell us which rooms, cupboards or items you want help with and which packing you will finish yourself. Include photos so the team can discuss the time and materials in your moving quote.

link.label: Choose the packing help you need

office-questions.title: Questions about a small office move

items.question: How is an office move priced?
items.answer: Office moves are quoted individually from the furniture, boxes, building access and timing. Send the inventory and floor plan with both addresses. List disassembly, packing and any unusual equipment so the quote covers the work you are asking for.

link.label: Send your office inventory for a quote

items.question: Who handles computer shutdown and reconnection?
items.answer: Arrange backups, shutdown, reconnection and network testing with your own IT provider. Tell the moving team which prepared devices need transport and agree the physical moving scope before the move.

link.label: Plan the office and IT handovers

items.question: Can the plan account for our building’s moving window?
items.answer: Send the approved loading and elevator windows for both buildings before agreeing on the schedule. Include the access contacts, loading entrance and COI requirements. Confirm the arrangement with the moving team and building management before telling staff when work can resume.

apartment-timeline.title: Plan the move in three passes

items.title: Before booking
items.text: Get both buildings’ access rules, moving windows and COI requirements.

items.title: While packing
items.text: Finish the item list, photograph awkward pieces and label boxes by room.

items.title: The day before
items.text: Walk the loading route, check the keys and confirm who opens each entrance.

apartment-handoff.title: Have these details ready for the crew
items: The complete item list and any packing help you want.
Building windows and a contact who can open the loading entrance.
Parking or loading arrangements at both addresses.
A plan for where large furniture goes at the new address.

coi-comparison.title: Two separate confirmations

items.title: Insurance paperwork
items.text: Send the building’s exact requirements to the mover. Management reviews the COI and confirms acceptance.

items.title: Elevator booking
items.text: Reserve the moving window with management. Confirm the entrance, access contact and elevator setup.

coi-comparison.note: An accepted COI does not reserve an elevator. An elevator booking does not confirm the insurance paperwork.

coi-checklist.title: Keep the access note together
items: Approved moving hours at pickup and delivery.
The service entrance and loading location.
Confirmation that required paperwork was accepted.
Elevator padding, keys and the person opening access.
A building contact who will answer during the move.

stairs-measurements.title: Measure the route, then the furniture
stairs-measurements.text: Check both addresses. These are the points to photograph and measure before the crew arrives.

items.title: Door opening
items.text: Measure the clear opening with the door open.

items.title: Stair width
items.text: Include handrails and any low ceiling.

items.title: Landing and turn
items.text: Show the space available to rotate a large piece.

stairs-measurements.note: A route sketch helps explain access; it cannot confirm that a particular piece will fit.

stairs-checklist.title: Before the stairway gets busy
items: Move shoes, plants and loose objects out of the carrying route.
Keep pets secure and shared doors accessible.
Mark furniture and boxes that stay behind.
Keep your essentials bag separate from the load.

kitchen-sort.title: Split the kitchen before you start

items.title: Keep in use
items.text: A few dishes, one pan, everyday utensils and your breakfast setup.
items.note: Pack these after the final meal.

items.title: Pack first
items.text: Serving dishes, spare glasses, occasional appliances and the cupboards you rarely open.
items.note: Work through one cupboard at a time.

kitchen-checklist.title: Before sealing a fragile box
items: The base is sound, taped and cushioned.
Each fragile piece is wrapped and separated.
Empty gaps are filled so pieces cannot knock together.
The box closes flat and can be carried safely.
The side is labeled with the room and contents.

office-roles.title: Give each part of the move an owner

items.title: Your move lead
items.text: Owns the inventory, building contacts and placement decisions. Names a backup.

items.title: Your IT provider
items.text: Handles backups, shutdown, reconnection and network testing as agreed.

items.title: The moving crew
items.text: Handles the physical move and furniture work within the agreed moving scope.

office-checklist.title: Ready for the first working morning
items: The move lead and backup can be reached.
The floor plan and labels use the same room or desk names.
IT has confirmed the reconnection and testing plan.
The receiving person has the inventory and access instructions.

inventory-example.title: Write an inventory someone else can use
inventory-example.text: Example format. Replace these sample entries with your own items, counts and measurements.

items.detail: Three-seat with chaise; add dimensions and note removable parts.
Add the bed size, storage drawers and disassembly needs.
Add a count or mark it approximate while packing continues.

inventory-checklist.title: Check the places a room list can miss
items: Closets, balcony and outdoor furniture.
Garage, storage cage or off-site storage.
Wall-mounted items and appliance parts.
Items added or removed since the last version.
Uncertain box counts, dates or destination access.

parking-comparison.title: Start with the person who controls the space

items.title: Private loading space
items.text: Ask building management about the dock, driveway or garage. Confirm booking, clearance and shared use.

items.title: Public curb space
items.text: Check with the authority responsible for the street. Confirm restrictions and any temporary-sign procedure directly.

parking-comparison.note: A postal address in Los Angeles does not establish which city controls the street.

parking-route.title: Show the whole route from truck to door

items.title: Loading point
items.text: Stopping position, approach and clearance.

items.title: Entrance
items.text: Correct street, gate and access contact.

items.title: Inside route
items.text: Lift, steps, corridors and tight turns.

items.title: Your door
items.text: Carry distance and the final opening.

packing-scope.title: Decide how much help you need

items.title: A room or selected items
items.text: Photograph the cupboards, shelves or fragile pieces you want help with. Say which packing you will finish yourself.

items.title: Packing across the home
items.text: Make a room-by-room list. Include storage areas and agree how packing time fits into the moving arrangement.

packing-scope.note: Tell us which packing tasks you want included. The quote should cover the time and any extra materials.

packing-materials.title: Agree the materials before moving day

items.title: Included moving supplies
items.text: Furniture blankets, wardrobe boxes for use during the move, tape and shrink wrap.

items.title: Confirm any extra charge
items.text: Boxes, bubble wrap and other additional materials. Ask which quantities your packing plan needs.

small-move-minimum.title: The two-mover minimum, before other charges

items.title: Cash
items.text: 3 hours × $115 per hour

items.title: Card
items.text: 3 hours × $125 per hour

small-move-minimum.note: Hourly-charge illustrations for two movers and a truck. The full quote also considers the route-based gas fee, driving-time terms, extra materials and actual work.
